pr_title: Remove SampleControlPoint and DifficultyControlPoint from HitObject
pr_body:
The purpose is to clean up the `HitObject` class by not allowing any redundant information to be stored by the `HitObject`.
- The slider velocity and tick generating information has been moved to `Slider` and got a separate interface for access.
- Legacy information is now property of the `HitObject`.
- Sample control point information gets applied to the `Samples` directly,  making the sample control point information completely obsolete.

fixes #22171 #22132 #15618 #19483
pr_comments: Test failures look very not promising at all.

Before dropping a review, huge thanks for taking on this effort. It's reassuring to have you both willing to understand and dive deep into the low-level structure of things surrounding hitobjects (which still have some work to get into a less-complex state).
You can probably close these issues as of the merging of this PR: https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/22132 https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/15618 https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/19483

issue_context.title: Exporting a beatmap to legacy creates an overabundance of inherited timing points
issue_context.body:
### Type

Game behaviour

### Bug description

Exporting a map from osu!lazer to import into stable creates an overabundance of timing points atop uninherited points (red points) as well as at the start and end of sliders.

comments: The reasoning here looks to be the flipflop between "normal" and "drum" sample sets. Could you please include or link the beatmap used to test this?

After further testing, it appears as if that was the issue. I imported a personal map from a friend, and was accidentally using hitnormals over drums. However, using `CTRL + A` to reassign every note to `drum` creates the same similar effect.

I've included a map directly exported from lazer where this occurs.

[Mai Zang - Si Ye Cao De Huang Xiang (Irisu)](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/234057206784458754/1063343143744974880/Mai_Zang_-_Si_Ye_Cao_De_Huan_Xiang_Irisu.osz)

I think it would be better if lazer assigns the sample sets directly onto the hitobjects instead of using timing points to do it.
This is also what the Map Cleaner tool does in Mapping Tools.
